name: Payload
tagline: A TypeScript CMS and application backend integrated with Next.js.
hook: Shows how the local API bypasses access control by default and why development mode cannot verify bundling changes.
summary: Payload's detailed instructions live in CLAUDE.md; AGENTS.md only points there. The guide covers CMS architecture and test fixtures, with examples for access control, React memoization, CSS, and server/client imports.

techniques.title: Make an unsafe default visible at the call site
techniques.body: Server functions and endpoints must supply both overrideAccess: false and the user to Payload operations. The guide contrasts a bare find call with the access-controlled form and explains the security consequence.
techniques.quote: **Building server functions, views, or endpoints:** Always use `overrideAccess: false` and pass the `user` to payload operations. Without these, the operation runs with access control disabled, which is a security vulnerability.

techniques.title: Put database lifecycle in the shared fixture
techniques.body: Integration tests use the repository's test wrapper instead of initializing Payload or seeding the database themselves. The fixture owns initialization, per-test reset, and cleanup, with an explicit exception for existing shared-state suites.
techniques.quote:
Do not initialize Payload manually or add database reset/seed hooks; the fixture initializes
  Payload once per file, resets and seeds before each test that uses it, and destroys it afterward

techniques.title: Make visual baselines reproducible across machines
techniques.body: Screenshot baselines must be generated inside the pinned Playwright Docker image. The reason is the effect of operating-system font rendering on comparisons, even when the UI has not changed.
techniques.quote:
**Baselines must be generated/updated inside the pinned Playwright Docker image**, never on a
  bare host — font rendering differs enough between operating systems to fail the comparison on
  CI even when nothing visually changed. Use `pnpm test:visual:update`.

techniques.title: Verify bundling in the mode where it can fail
techniques.body: The server/client import rules explain why relative imports and barrel exports can cause production-only problems. The required verification builds and serves production output rather than relying on the dev server.
techniques.quote: **Testing bundling changes:** Always test with `pnpm prepare-run-test-against-prod` followed by `pnpm dev:prod <suite>`. Dev mode (`pnpm dev`) doesn't catch these issues.

techniques.title: Show physical and logical CSS properties side by side
techniques.body: A bad/good pair replaces left and right properties with inline-direction equivalents. The example makes the RTL requirement concrete across spacing, borders, and positioning.

steal: Identify security-sensitive defaults and the parameters that override them.
Give shared test fixtures clear ownership of setup and cleanup.
Pin the environment used to generate visual baselines.
Map production-only failure modes to production-mode checks.
